title: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti
hook: Sanjaya arrives from the blind king with a message about peace, and Yudhishthira answers with a very small request
carry: five villages, and let this end
tomorrow: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti

segments.voice: Yesterday: Udyoga, the getting ready, began at Krishna's bedside, and Arjuna chose Krishna over an army. Your line was whose face Krishna saw when he opened his eyes.

An envoy rides into the Pandava camp. It's Sanjaya, the trusted charioteer and counselor of the blind king Dhritarashtra. He greets everyone warmly, asks after their health, and then delivers his master's message. It isn't an offer. It isn't a threat. It's a plea: don't fight. And something is missing from it. Dhritarashtra asks for peace, but he doesn't offer to give back what was taken.
screen: `SANJAYA RIDES IN.` → `THE MESSAGE: DON'T FIGHT.` → `WHAT THE MESSAGE LEAVES OUT.`

segments.voice: Sanjaya speaks movingly, and the Pandavas don't brush it aside. A war between cousins, he says, means killing your own teachers, your own uncles, your own kin. What kind of victory is that? Better, he says, to live on alms than to win a kingdom that way. Yudhishthira's answer is not angry. I want peace too, he says. Who would choose war if peace were possible? But peace has to mean something. Give us back our own kingdom, Indraprastha, the city we built. Krishna speaks as well. Holding back from action, he says, is no answer by itself; a person must act, and act rightly. In Krishna's reply, Sanjaya's advice sounds holy but asks only one side to give anything up. And then, in this same exchange, Yudhishthira makes a request so small it's almost painful to hear. Not the whole kingdom. Not even the city. Give us five villages, he says, and let this end. Five villages, from men who once ruled. Sanjaya carries the message home. Stay with the shape of the exchange. One side talks about peace as the absence of fighting. The other talks about peace as fairness, and will accept very little of it.
screen: `SANJAYA: DON'T FIGHT YOUR KIN` · `YUDHISHTHIRA: WE WANT PEACE TOO` · `KRISHNA: ACT, AND ACT RIGHTLY` · then, large: `EVEN FIVE VILLAGES`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a disagreement you're in, at home, at work, with a friend. Breathing in, ask what fairness would look like here, for both of you; breathing out, ask what's the smallest thing that would let you make peace, and let the two questions sit side by side without deciding anything. If you pray, you can bring that disagreement into your prayer.
Udyoga. The getting ready, where an envoy asks for peace, and Yudhishthira asks for five villages.
Your line: five villages, and let this end. Peace that's fair, even if it's small. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Yudhishthira's request for five villages is remembered in retellings of the Mahabharata as the very small price the Pandavas would accept for peace before the war.

pairs: better alms than a kingdom won by killing

fork.setup: you're Yudhishthira. Sanjaya says war with your kin would be a terrible wrong, but offers nothing back. what do you answer?
options: agree, and stay in exile for good.
say you want peace too, and ask for your kingdom, or even five villages.
send Sanjaya away without an answer.
fork.reveal: he answers gently, asks for Indraprastha, and then for as little as five villages.

original.note: effort, getting ready; the book where both sides prepare, and envoys travel between them.

trapdoor: what you thought: Sanjaya was the peacemaker and the Pandavas wanted war.
what it means: Sanjaya asks only one side to give up its claim; Yudhishthira also wants peace, but a fair one.
what a scholar hears: 'five villages' shrinks the dispute to its plainest terms, and shows how little the Pandavas would accept.
guess: getting ready, where both sides weigh peace and war
a royal envoy sent to carry a king's message
the five villages the Pandavas asked to keep

chat.says: If Sanjaya came to ask for peace, why didn't the Pandavas just agree?
options: They wanted peace too, but a fair one: their kingdom back, or even just five villages.
They had already sworn to fight and wouldn't listen to anyone from the Kuru court.
Sanjaya came only to spy on their camp, not to bring a message.
chat.meaning: Yudhishthira says he wants peace too, but peace has to mean something. He asks for Indraprastha, then for only five villages.

Sanjaya.meaning: Dhritarashtra's charioteer and counselor, sent as envoy

Dhritarashtra.meaning: the blind Kuru king, father of Duryodhana

Indraprastha.meaning: the city the Pandavas built and ruled

Udyoga.meaning: effort, getting ready; the book of the epic before the war

Krishna.meaning: Arjuna's cousin and friend, revered by many Hindus as divine

recall: truthful son with a year left to live
